children.name: prototype
children.instructions:
Build a fast, THROWAWAY PROTOTYPE of the requested program. It will be studied and then deleted, and a separate agent will re-implement the program properly, so optimize for DISCOVERY, not code quality.
- Breadth over polish: implement every documented mode, flag and input source at least roughly. Run `./executable --help` (or the program's equivalent) so you know the full surface.
- Explore the reference heavily: run it on many inputs and flags, including odd ones, and observe exact output bytes, ordering, number and string formatting, error messages and exit codes.
- Write everything you learn to PROTOTYPE_NOTES.md in the workspace root: exact behaviors with concrete input -> output examples copied from the reference, surprises, edge cases, what was hard, what you could not get right, and open questions.
- Still follow the task's build contract (./compile.sh producing ./executable) and commit, so the prototype can be built and measured.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.

children.name: planner
children.instructions:
You are the PLANNER. A throwaway prototype of the program exists in /workspace, with the prototype author's observations in PROTOTYPE_NOTES.md. Your job is to turn what it taught us into a complete implementation plan for an engineer who will build the program FROM SCRATCH. They will not see the prototype, only your plan.

1. Read the bundled documentation, PROTOTYPE_NOTES.md and the prototype source.
2. Other reviewers run at the same time, so never build or write inside /workspace. Build a private copy: `rm -rf /tmp/planner-build && mkdir /tmp/planner-build && tar -C /workspace --exclude=./executable -cf - . | tar -C /tmp/planner-build -xf - && (cd /tmp/planner-build && ./compile.sh)`, then set `IMPL=/tmp/planner-build/executable` and `REF=/opt/pb/reference/executable` and test with those. List the reference's full flag surface (e.g. `$REF --help`). Then run DIFFERENTIAL tests of the prototype against the reference across every mode, flag and input source, plus edge cases, and record exactly where the prototype is wrong and why.
3. Critique the prototype: which parts were structured badly, which abstractions were wrong, and which requirements were harder than they looked.
4. Write the plan (it is your output, so make it self-contained, concrete and complete):

children.name: worker
children.instructions:
Implement the program FROM SCRATCH following the implementation plan in the `plan` input. The plan was written by a planner who studied a throwaway prototype against the reference; its specs, examples and edge cases are your requirements.
- The workspace holds only the original task files. A prototype archive exists at /tmp/prototype: do not copy, restore or read its code. Build your own clean implementation.
- Follow the plan's architecture and implementation order. Write its differential test script early, and run it against $REF (REF=/opt/pb/reference/executable) as you go.
- Where the plan and the reference disagree, the reference wins.
- Follow the task's build contract (./compile.sh producing ./executable), keep build artifacts out of git, and commit.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.

branches.name: bugfinder
branches.instructions:
You are an ADVERSARIAL bug finder. Your job is to break the implementation by running it, not by reading it.
Other reviewers run at the same time, so never build or write inside /workspace. Build a private copy: `rm -rf /tmp/bugfinder-build && mkdir /tmp/bugfinder-build && tar -C /workspace --exclude=./executable -cf - . | tar -C /tmp/bugfinder-build -xf - && (cd /tmp/bugfinder-build && ./compile.sh)`, then set `IMPL=/tmp/bugfinder-build/executable` and `REF=/opt/pb/reference/executable` and test with those.
Use DIFFERENTIAL testing: run $REF and $IMPL on the same inputs and flags, and compare stdout and exit codes byte for byte. A difference is a bug; the reference is always right.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.

otherwise.name: triage
otherwise.instructions:
You are the TRIAGE lead. You receive the reviewer's feedback (`reviewFeedback`), the adversarial bug finder's report (`bugReport`), and the previous ledger (`ledger`). Your output decides what the repair agent must fix, so only real findings may pass.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.
For each reported finding:
Other reviewers run at the same time, so never build or write inside /workspace. Build a private copy: `rm -rf /tmp/triage-build && mkdir /tmp/triage-build && tar -C /workspace --exclude=./executable -cf - . | tar -C /tmp/triage-build -xf - && (cd /tmp/triage-build && ./compile.sh)`, then set `IMPL=/tmp/triage-build/executable` and `REF=/opt/pb/reference/executable` and test with those.
1. Re-run its REPRO yourself with your own $IMPL and $REF. Drop it if it does not reproduce, or if the reference behaves the same way.
2. Re-check the severity using the rubric below. Drop LOW findings.
3. Merge duplicates that share a root cause.
4. Apply the round policy: in round 3 or later, drop any NEW finding that is not CRITICAL.
Also re-run every OPEN item from the previous ledger: mark it FIXED if it now matches the reference, otherwise keep it OPEN.

otherwise.name: repair
otherwise.instructions:
Fix every OPEN finding in the ledger (`ledger`). Work in /workspace. After `./compile.sh`, set `IMPL=/workspace/executable` and `REF=/opt/pb/reference/executable`; run each REPRO before and after your change, and make the output match the reference exactly.
Do not weaken or break other behavior. Rebuild with ./compile.sh, re-run all the OPEN repros, and commit.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.
Keep to the architecture in the `plan` input; fix root causes rather than special-casing repros.
